title: Civic and community engagement among health profession students and professionals compared to the general population: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
content:
by Aria Ghasedi, Ramin Vahidi

Background

Physicians, nurses, and other health professionals encounter poverty, inequality, and the structural roots of ill health as a routine part of clinical work — an exposure that differs from that of most other occupations. The World Health Organization, the Global Consensus for Social Accountability of Medical Schools, and many professional bodies describe civic and community engagement as a professional responsibility. Whether health profession students and practitioners show higher, lower, or comparable levels of civic engagement relative to the broader public in non-crisis conditions has not been systematically reviewed. The existing literature is fragmented, limited to single professions, focused largely on pandemic volunteerism, and more concerned with attitudes than with behaviour.

Methods

We present a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting behavioural civic and community engagement among health profession students and practising professionals across all disciplines, with or without a general-population or non-health comparator. Seven databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, ERIC, PsycINFO, and Embase) and grey-literature sources will be searched from inception without date or language restrictions. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and assess risk of bias using JBI checklists matched to prevalence and comparative analyses (and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies), together with an appraisal of measurement-instrument quality. Within pre-specified, conceptually comparable analysis groups, prevalence will be pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models, and odds ratios and standardized mean differences with restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; prediction intervals will be reported. Certainty of evidence will be graded with GRADE, separately for prevalence and between-group comparisons. Reporting will follow PRISMA 2020.

Expected outputs

No results are yet available; the review is at the protocol stage. The completed review will report pooled prevalence of each engagement domain, unadjusted and adjusted comparisons with general-population, education-matched, and non-health student comparators, and the certainty of evidence for each estimate.

Discussion

This work will produce the first cross-disciplinary behavioural benchmark of civic engagement across the health professions relative to the general public, with implications for how social accountability is taught, evaluated, and valued within health professions education and practice.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO CRD420261348391.
